doc.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995

title: Charlie Parker's effect on alto playing
summary: He credits Parker with changing alto style, though he heard Benny Carter as a pioneer and heard Parker in Kansas City before his style matured with Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: As a alto sax player, can you relate to anything, relate for us anything that the innovations that came on the scene when Charlie Parker came on the scene?
How did he change the way that alto sax players played?

Well Charlie gets credit for that see? Of pioneering in a new style. Firstly, I’ve heard Benny Carter play so much when he was young, see? And I always thought Benny was a pioneer also. He started at, particularly at that period. But I give Charlie the credit of changing the scene in alto playing. But you know he did most of that when he arrived in New York. I heard him in Kansas City with Jay McShann. He wasn’t playing exactly the same way. He was still, you could hear edges of his style coming out, but it wasn’t perfected until he got associated in New York City with Dizzy. That’s when it came out see?
